title: Customer credential rotation & audit synopsis
summary: Working draft: spec for customer-side credential (TLS/KMS) rotation in Private deployments, the approval gates required for production change windows, and a compact, tamper-evident audit-log schema for rotation events that customers and Redwood can consume.
problem_statement: Customers running Private (VPC / on-prem) instances run their own network edge and often manage certificates, API keys, or hardware-backed keys. There is no standardized flow today for safe, auditable key/certificate rotation that handles: operator approval, cross-checks with Redwood control plane, and tamper-evident retention for compliance audits. This causes ad-hoc scripts, inconsistent retention, and operational risk during rollovers (partial rotations, stale keys, failed rollbacks).
goals: Define a safe, reversible rotation flow for customer-managed TLS certs, API keys, and KMS-wrapped secrets
Specify approval gates for production rotations (automated vs human-in-the-loop) with clear escalation rules
Design an audit-log schema that is compact, signed, and supports replay-detection and retention policy enforcement
Provide an operator UX sketch (console + CLI) and an API contract so solutions engineers can automate handoffs
Ensure the design is compatible with common customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM) and with Redwood private control plane attestation hooks
non_goals: Implementing a full certificate lifecycle manager (we integrate with existing customer tooling)
Replacing customer KMS or key escrow policies
Solving every edge-case for multi-region BYO network topologies in this doc
proposed_design:
Overview:
- Two-tier rotation model: 1) Local rotation (customer-initiated, low-risk items like API keys tied to dev workflows) and 2) Production rotation (TLS certs, root HSM keys) which require approval gates.

Flow (production rotation):
1) Customer/Operator creates a rotation request via Console or CLI with: resource_type (cert|api-key|kms-key), resource_id, target_material (public cert, new key ID), scheduled_window, rollback_strategy, operator_notes.
2) Request is assigned a short immutable request_id. The control plane returns a pre-signed challenge and audit metadata blob to be included in rotation operation on the customer appliance.
3) Customer appliance performs the swap locally (install cert / rotate key) and submits a signed assertion: {request_id, resource_id, before_hash, after_hash, timestamp, nonce, operator_key_id}. The assertion must be signed by a key the customer admits is valid (HSM or operator key).
4) Redwood validates assertion signature, verifies that the challenge nonce matches, and runs policy checks (downtime SLO, dependency map). If policy passes, the request transitions to APPROVED. If policy fails or is ambiguous, it transitions to PENDING and triggers human review (notified to on-call and customer delegates).
5) Approval gate types: automatic (policy), delegated (pre-approved operator list), or manual (requires sign-off from two seats). Approval actions are recorded in the audit log and produce a signed Redwood approval token.
6) Finalization: customer appliance polls for approval token, attaches it to the final commit, and the control plane stores the rotation event in the tamper-evident audit log for the agreed retention window.

Design notes:
- Every submitted assertion and every Redwood approval is recorded as an atomic event. Events are chained with a running SHA256 hash (like a lightweight Merkle chain) so that log tampering is detectable.
- Logs include minimal PII; where necessary, sensitive payloads are stored encrypted with a customer-wrapped key and only a reference is kept in the main log.
- The control plane exposes a read-only, signed log export endpoint for customers and auditors. Exports are timestamped and include a signature that can be verified offline.

Audit retention & storage options:
- Default retention: 365 days compressed.
- Compliance-tier retention options: 7 years (legal hold) available as an add-on.
- Storage backends: object store with server-side encryption, optional customer-provided KMS wrapping for at-rest encryption of sensitive fields.

Failure modes & rollback:
- If appliance fails to apply new material before scheduled_window_end, the request auto-rollbacks to previous material using signed rollback token stored in a secure vault (short-lived).
- Partial failures: the system supports a staged rollout tag (canary %) and automated reversion for health-check failures.

APIs:
- POST /rotation-requests -> {request_id}
- GET /rotation-requests/{id}/status -> {status, events[]}
- POST /rotation-requests/{id}/assert -> {signed_assertion}
- POST /rotation-requests/{id}/approve -> {approval_token}
- GET /audit-log?from=&to=&resource_id= -> signed-compact-log (ndjson)
audit_log_schema:
Conceptual: ndjson, each line is a signed event. Fields: timestamp, event_id, type, resource_type, resource_id, actor (redwood|customer), actor_key_id, prev_hash, event_payload_reference, signature, retention_tier. Sample event types: ROTATION_REQUEST_CREATED, TOKEN_CHALLENGE_ISSUED, ASSERTION_SUBMITTED, POLICY_CHECK_RESULT, APPROVAL_GRANTED, ROLLBACK_EXECUTED. Example event (plaintext line): {
  "timestamp": "2025-01-15T17:22:03Z",
  "event_id": "rr-20250115-0003",
  "type": "ASSERTION_SUBMITTED",
  "resource_type": "tls-cert",
  "resource_id": "customer-edge-01",
  "actor": "customer",
  "actor_key_id": "hsm-az1-22",
  "prev_hash": "e3b0c442...",
  "event_payload_reference": "s3://redwood-logs/rot/2025/01/15/payload-rr-3.enc",
  "signature": "MEUCIQD...",
  "retention_tier": "standard-365"
}

Operational properties:
- Compact: payloads > 1kB are uploaded to encrypted blob store and referenced.
- Signed: events are signed by the originating actor and by Redwood for cross-trust verification.
- Chainable: each event references prev_hash to make tampering detectable.
- Replay-resilient: nonces + sequence numbers prevent naive replay attacks.
- Privacy: PII/sensitive material encrypted with customer-wrapped keys where requested.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end rotation for TLS certs works in canary mode with automatic rollback on health-check failures
Audit export verifies signatures and prev_hash chain for a 30-day window
Delegated approval lists can be configured and enforced for at least 3 seats
Control plane can attach customer-wrapped encryption keys to sensitive payloads and later decrypt only with customer consent (integration test)
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (internal alpha): wiring on-prem infra team + CLI hooks, run 5 internal rotations against staging appliances.
Phase 1 (beta customers): opt-in with 3 customers with varied topology (AWS VPC, GCP VPC, on-prem HSM). Monitor failures, mean-time-to-rollback, and audit proof generation.
Phase 2 (general availability): enable default UI, add retention tiering purchase option, and provide runbook templates for customer SRE.

Metrics to track:
- rotation_success_rate, mean_time_to_approve, mean_time_to_rollback, audit_export_latency, signed_events_per_rotation
open_questions: Should Redwood store full assertions (encrypted) or only references by default?
What SLAs do we offer for audit export (near-real-time vs batched daily)?
How do we handle cross-account validation when customer appliance uses an air-gapped HSM with intermittent connectivity?
Can we reuse existing attestation APIs or do we need a distinct rotation assertion protocol?
notes_to_self: Driver: align with legal on retention tiers before presenting to customers. Schedule sync with infra (Miguel) to validate HSM signing support. Prioritize sample scripts for CLI flow; these will be the easiest onboarding artifact for Solutions Engineering. Keep UX minimal for beta (console + simple JSON payload).
